acceptance.given: Declared repair and runtime evidence boundaries exist and historical evidence content is retained as an immutable baseline.

oracle.expected: The boundary check shows new evidence only as appended content within declared boundaries while prior evidence bytes remain retained.
oracle.observable: Pre-write and post-write evidence-boundary comparison performed by the toolchain evidence handler.

acceptance.then: Repair and runtime evidence is append-only within declared boundaries and historical evidence remains unchanged.
acceptance.when: The toolchain records repair or runtime evidence and evaluates the write boundary.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Attempt an evidence write that overwrites, deletes, or escapes its declared append-only boundary.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce append-only evidence recording within declared boundaries and reject overwrite, deletion, or out-of-bound evidence writes.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Existing historical evidence remains immutable; evidence-record representation changes must remain append-only and non-authorizing.

slice_hint.state_transition: retained historical evidence and declared boundary -> attempted repair/runtime evidence recording -> appended in-bound evidence or rejected integrity violation
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The boundary comparison proves retained prior evidence and permits only appended repair/runtime evidence within the declared boundary.

acceptance.given: A Current Snapshot records the identities of result-determining inputs for a prior replay result.

oracle.expected: Before semantic reproduction is accepted, reconstruction detects a changed snapshot-bound input and returns stale or another fail-closed result.
forbidden: A changed bound input is silently normalized away without an approved versioned policy.
A stale result is reported as reproduced or successful.
oracle.observable: The Toolchain replay reconstruction result and its bound-input identity comparison are evaluated before semantic reproduction.

acceptance.then: The prior result is invalidated and no semantic-reproduction claim is accepted.
acceptance.when: During Current Snapshot reconstruction and before launching or accepting fresh replay evidence.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Mutate one result-determining snapshot member and require the reconstruction check to reject any non-stale reproduction result.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Compare every reconstructed result-determining bound input with its Current Snapshot identity and fail closed as stale before semantic reproduction.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve snapshot compatibility; a changed bound identity invalidates only the dependent prior result.

slice_hint.state_transition: snapshot-bound prior result -> identity reconstruction -> stale fail-closed result on unexplained drift
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Any unexplained mismatch in a result-determining snapshot member prevents semantic reproduction and yields stale or another fail-closed terminal status.

acceptance.given: A Replay Result succeeds for an input whose Validator Capability is independently evaluable.

oracle.expected: The replay result includes a Validator Capability verification outcome produced for that result, independently of other replay verifications.
forbidden: A successful Replay Result whose Validator Capability verification is inferred from another verification.
oracle.observable: The successful replay result's per-result Validator Capability verification outcome.

acceptance.then: The successful Replay Result carries its own Validator Capability verification outcome.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the S24 replay behavior test with a successful replay whose Validator Capability outcome is omitted or borrowed; the runtime assertion must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require each successful replay result to independently verify and expose its Validator Capability outcome.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Restore prior replay-result verification handling without changing the capability descriptor schema.

slice_hint.state_transition: successful replay without independent capability verification -> successful replay with a per-result independent capability outcome
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The S24 selector rejects a successful replay that lacks its own Validator Capability verification.

acceptance.given: A proposed implementation scope is evaluated as TC-D1 work and includes TC-E0 or TC-D2 through TC-D6 implementation.

oracle.expected: The Toolchain plan validator rejects the proposed scope as outside TC-D1.
forbidden: Acceptance of TC-E0 implementation as TC-D1 work.
Acceptance of TC-D2, TC-D3, TC-D4, TC-D5, or TC-D6 implementation as TC-D1 work.
oracle.observable: The validator returns a failing scope decision identifying the excluded roadmap implementation request.

acceptance.then: TC-E0 and TC-D2 through TC-D6 implementation scope is rejected.
acceptance.when: When determining whether proposed work is within TC-D1 scope.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Exercise the plan validator with an isolated roadmap fixture containing TC-E0 and TC-D2 through TC-D6 implementation identifiers; accepting any identifier fails the boundary assertion.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Extend the Toolchain plan validator so TC-E0 and TC-D2 through TC-D6 implementation requests are deterministically rejected as outside TC-D1 scope.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Revert only the TC-D1 scope-classification addition; retain roadmap ownership, lifecycle authority, historical records, and all protected boundaries.

slice_hint.state_transition: Roadmap scope has not yet been checked against TC-D1 boundaries. -> TC-E0 and TC-D2 through TC-D6 implementation scope is rejected.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The Toolchain plan validator rejects every proposed TC-D1 implementation scope that contains TC-E0 or TC-D2 through TC-D6 implementation work.
